title: attenuated-scale-drift-corrector-and-kv-prefetch-adapter-for-quant-paths
author: Maya Chen
body: Motivation: We observed subtle per-head scale drift when fusing dequant+attention kernels for mixed INT8/FP8 inference on long-context workloads. The drift reduces softmax stability and causes quality jitter at tail tokens, forcing either conservative dequant choices or pay-for-precision fallbacks. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) an attenuated-scale drift correction pass in the quant fusion pipeline that applies a calibrated per-head attenuation and lightweight renormalization to preserve numeric stability when fusing dequant + attn; and 2) a KV-prefetch adapter that warms KV cache for fused fast-path microkernels to avoid cold-start p99 spikes during continuous batching and interactive patterns. Design: - attenuated_scale_pass: a compiler/pipeline pass that inserts a small per-head multiplicative correction (scale attenuation + bias adjust) when the fusion identifies asymmetric per-head ranges. The pass emits metadata so that runtime microkernels can choose a fast-path that avoids a full recompute of scales. The correction is designed to be idempotent and toggled via model config or per-route rollout flags. - requant microkernel (kernels/requant_vperm.S): adds a vectorized requantization path optimized for AVX-512/ARM SVE that uses lane-aligned vperm and fused mad instructions to reduce scalar renormalize ops. The kernel returns a compact scale tag consumed by the runtime. - kv_prefetch_adapter (scheduler/kv_prefetch_adapter.cc): a scheduler hook that observes continuous batch characteristics (steady-state token rate, active prefixes) and proactively issues lightweight KV fetches for expected upcoming prefixes using the model's prefix-hash hints. It is conservative (deadline-aware) and disabled for GPU memory-constrained pools. - runtime integration: runtime/quant/attenuated_scale_pass.cpp wires pass metadata through the model descriptor and runtime/runtime_kv_bridge picks fast-path kernels when metadata present. Rollout plan: 1) opt-in per-model by default off 2) staged canary on dedicated clusters 3) gradual rollout to hosted after 2 weeks of canary metrics Observed results (internal bench): - Llama-13B INT8-smoothed baseline vs this PR: p99 latency down ~18% on interactive traces, median latency up to 10% improved for short sequences, overall throughput +27% at 95th percentile load. - Token-level quality regression: negligible on our eval prompt set (<0.2% BLEU-like drift), with occasional alignment differences on adversarial prompts (added to eval set). Tests and QA: - unit tests for attenuated_scale_pass and microkernel correctness included. - end-to-end integration test simulates continuous batching + KV warmup. - bench/bench_quant_prefetch.py reproduces p99 improvements in CI perf job (internal). Checklist: - [x] Implementation of attenuated-scale pass and microkernel - [x] Scheduler KV-prefetch adapter - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmarks and perf dashboards updated - [x] Docs note added (docs/notes/quant-prefetch.md) Security/compatibility notes: - No change to model weights. - New runtime metadata is backward compatible; fallback to existing dequant path if microkernel not available. - Feature guarded behind rollout flag. Related work: ENG-1289 (quant stability), ENG-1310 (kv cache p99), SUP-4421 (customer-reported cold-start p99 incident).

merge_outcome: Merged by squash on 2026-02-28 after 3 approvals. Merge method: squash. Release notes: Adds attenuated-scale drift-correction pass and a KV prefetch scheduler adapter to improve INT8/FP8 fused attention stability and p99 latency; opt-in behind model config and rollout flag.
release_notes: Add attenuated-scale drift-correction pass for quant fusion and KV-prefetch adapter to reduce cold-start p99; opt-in via model config. See docs/notes/quant-prefetch.md for rollout and troubleshooting.
notes_for_ops: Enable 'quant_drift.disable' in runtime config to revert to previous dequant path. Can be toggled per-deployment. Watch metrics: quant/attn/p99_latency and kv/prefetch/hit_rate.
